inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted 138,602k from FY2026 Annual Report Note 8 (basic 137,675k + share rights); held FLAT - SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge. Buyback paused since Feb-2025; management flags a possible buyback after the FY27 interim.
inputs.net_debt_basis: NET CASH of $79.1m. Lease treatment (B): total_debt of $62.5m is ENTIRELY lease liabilities (30.521 current + 31.962 non-current) and is EXCLUDED from net debt, because lease principal is instead deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct. Sky has had zero bank borrowings since FY2023. Charging leases in both places would double-count them.
inputs.owner_fcf_basis: Owner FCF = Sky's own normalised free cash flow $58.9m less interest income $1.753m = $57.15m. Sky defines normalised FCF as OCF - lease principal - capex, excluding one-offs, and normalises for the nil tax actually paid (-$15.2m). The CSV's reported FCF of $89.3m is OCF-capex only: it deducts no lease principal, includes the $8.2m Optus receipt, and reflects nil cash tax.

fcf_bridge.item: Sky's stated FY26 free cash flow
add back Sky Free integration incl capex
add back Optus customer credits and capex
tax normalisation (nil tax paid in FY26 is not repeatable)
less interest income (net cash sits in the bridge)
Owner FCF base used in this model

inputs.revenue_base_basis: FY2026 UNDERLYING revenue $826.1m, not reported $824.8m. Underlying EBITDA $157.0m (margin 19.0%), underlying NPAT $41.8m.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based payment $0.396m (FY2026 not separately disclosed; immaterial). NZX-typical near-zero SBC - rows kept explicit per the SBC-zero rule.
inputs.nci_note: Non-controlling interest is immaterial: $0.423m of FY26 profit (0.7% of NPAT) and $1.708m of equity. Not modelled separately; flows are effectively attributable.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-28 NZX regular close (verified live from Yahoo). 52-week range 3.02-3.66 - the stock is near its 52-week HIGH, at 83% of the range.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md - Sky is an operating company (media/broadcasting) whose value is a stream of free cash flow, so the owner-FCF engine plus the section 7 non-US adaptations applies. Section 7 items engaged: (a) NZD-matched WACC; (b) ONE lease treatment - (B), principal in the flows, lease liabilities out of net debt; (c) NCI immaterial, charged once (not deducted); (d) interest income stripped because net cash is in the bridge; (e) SBC-zero market, band_position null; (f) risk charged ONCE - structural decline and rights risk live in the FLOWS, only illiquidity and single-country premiums are in the WACC.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company guidance (revenue $825-840m vs FY26 underlying $826.1m, midpoint +0.8%), NOT a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs are unreliable as forward proxies here. Revenue 5yr CAGR of 3.0% is ACQUISITION-driven (Discovery NZ from 1 Aug 2025 added ~$70m); organic revenue is flat-to-declining. EPS 5yr CAGR of 74% runs off a near-zero FY2021 base and FY2026 is inflated by the $31.4m bargain-purchase gain. Owner-FCF CAGRs of 27-64% are artefacts of a FY2021-2025 trough depressed by the Optus satellite-migration capex supercycle. Forward growth is anchored to guidance instead.

wacc_rationale.currency_basis: NZD - built from the NZ 10-year government bond and a NZ equity risk premium, matching the currency of the flows.

premiums.reason: 100% New Zealand, ~5m population, no geographic diversification

wacc_rationale.capital_structure: Zero bank debt since FY2023 and a net cash balance sheet, so WACC = cost of equity; there is no debt tranche to weight.
wacc_rationale.risk_charged_once: Per section 7(f), structural satellite decline, NZR content-rights risk and Sky Free integration risk are charged in the FLOWS (negative organic growth in every scenario, a rights-loss bear case, synergies discounted in base and nil in bear) and are deliberately NOT also added to the discount rate. The same WACC of 13.0% is used in all three scenarios - varying it per scenario would charge risk a third time.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands inside guidance (revenue $825-840m, EBITDA $155-165m) and Sky Free synergies reach the promised $10m+ by FY28, holding revenue roughly flat for three years and lifting the EBITDA margin from 19.0% to about 20.5%. From FY2030 the arithmetic of the core reasserts itself: Sky Box is ~54% of revenue and shrinking 5-8% a year, and streaming, advertising and broadband are too small to offset it, so group revenue drifts to -1.5%/yr and the margin eases back as the mix shifts toward lower-margin advertising and free-to-air. The cheaper NZR deal (~$75-80m/yr vs ~$111m) is a genuine and durable margin support, and capex normalises to the guided 7% of revenue now the Optus satellite migration is finished.
scenario_narratives.bull: Sky Free is the pivot management says it is: advertising and BVOD scale on the acquired Three/ThreeNow inventory, digital advertising compounds off its small base, broadband keeps growing ~15%, and together they genuinely offset satellite attrition so group revenue grows ~1.5-2%/yr toward the stated FY2031 ambition of 20-30% of revenue from non-subscription sources. Synergies exceed $10m, programming costs settle at the 47% end of the 47-49% target, and the EBITDA margin reaches 23% - above the 21-23% three-year target Sky has so far missed. Capex falls to the bottom of the 6-8% envelope. Even here the exit is capped at 5.6x EV/EBITDA, the highest multiple this market has paid in a decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: The satellite base decays faster than 5-8% as households cut discretionary spend in a weak NZ economy, and Neon keeps shrinking against a standalone HBO Max that launched in NZ on 16 June 2026 after Sky chose not to renew exclusivity. The acquired free-to-air business is a declining linear-advertising asset in a market that fell 11% in FY25, and integration synergies are consumed by content inflation rather than dropping to EBITDA. Because the satellite cost base is largely fixed - transponder, field technicians, set-top hardware - a shrinking subscriber base produces operating deleverage, so the margin falls from 19% to 13.5%. The 2030 NZR renewal reprices against Sky again, or fragments further to a global streamer. Revenue declines ~4.5%/yr and terminal growth is negative.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is raised to 30% from the 15% house default because the central risk here is structural, not cyclical: the majority of revenue sits in a satellite base that has declined every single reporting period for five years, and the designated replacement growth engine (Neon) is itself now shrinking. Bull is cut to 20% because it requires several independent things to go right at once - synergies exceeding target, an advertising turnaround in a market that is contracting, AND a margin above a 21-23% target Sky has already missed twice. Base holds 50%: FY2027 guidance is credible and near-term visibility is good.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Null by the SBC-zero rule: share-based payment is ~0.05% of revenue, so the house and street bases coincide (weighted $3.49 vs $3.51) and the band collapses to a point. Reporting a percentage position inside a 2-cent band would be spurious.

entry_price.method: PV of the interim owner-FCF path at 15%, plus the scenario terminal value (computed at WACC, capped) discounted at 15%, plus net cash, per share.

required_return_table.note: Base-case value per share at each required return. At the current price of $3.55 the market is pricing roughly a 13% required return - i.e. today's buyer is being paid about the model's WACC and no more.

sensitivity.note: Base case. The 11% WACC row flattens at higher terminal growth because the 3.0x EV/EBITDA exit-multiple cap binds - the guardrail preventing the model from paying a multiple this market has never paid.

investigated_but_not_tripped: Implied P/E of 12.04x on underlying EPS sits just above the 10-year P/E range top of 11.5x, but well inside the 2.0x-of-average (14.8x) formal trip threshold. Noted rather than ignored: it means the base case already assumes a mild re-rating above anything the last decade has paid.

Implied P/B of 1.08x exceeds the 10-year maximum of 1.01x that Sky has NEVER traded above, though it is inside the 1.5x-of-max (1.52x) trip threshold. The current price of $3.55 itself implies 1.05x book, so the market - not the model - is the party paying an unprecedented multiple.

Base-year peak test: the normalised owner-FCF base of $57.1m is 2.47x the seven-year median of $23.1m, which trips the 1.5x peak-extrapolation screen. Investigated and resolved: the FY2021-2025 trough was depressed by the Optus satellite-migration capex supercycle (capex $71-89m against a guided $60-65m steady state) and by $19.7m of accelerated content amortisation in FY2025, and the base is independently corroborated by FY2027 guidance - a bottom-up build at the guidance midpoint gives $52.7m against the model's year-1 $53.5m. The base is a guided figure, not an extrapolated peak.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No formal trip. The model was built from the outset on UNDERLYING FY2026 figures and on Sky's own normalised free cash flow, with a 28% normalised tax rate replacing the nil tax actually paid, so the usual failure mode (extrapolating an inflated reported base) was avoided rather than corrected after the fact.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Preventative, applied during construction rather than after a trip: (1) underlying not reported earnings as the base; (2) Sky's own normalised FCF less interest income as the owner-FCF anchor; (3) 28% cash tax modelled throughout despite nil tax paid in FY2026; (4) structural WACC premiums of +250bp for illiquidity and single-country concentration; (5) Step 8c exit-multiple caps on terminal value - bear 1.9x (10yr min), base 3.0x (recent-range top), bull 5.6x (10yr max) EV/EBITDA. The Gordon value was below the cap in all three scenarios, so the caps bound nothing but stand as a guardrail.

valuation_philosophy.underlying_vs_reported: Reported FY2026 is not the earnings power of this business. Statutory NPAT of $59.8m contains a $31.4m non-cash gain on bargain purchase from acquiring Discovery NZ for a nominal $1 (note: $31.4m final, revised down from the $34.4m provisional figure carried in the H1 interim) and $8.2m of Optus satellite-migration compensation, partly offset by $13.9m of Sky Free integration and transaction costs. Underlying NPAT is $41.8m, and it grew just 1.8% year on year - despite consolidating an entire acquired business. Reported EBITDA of $170.2m against underlying $157.0m tells the same story, and the apparent +41% EBITDA jump from FY2025 is an artefact of a weak base ($19.7m of accelerated content amortisation) plus the one-off gain; underlying growth was +5.8%. Reported FCF of $89.3m is flattered three ways: it deducts no lease principal ($26.1m), it includes the $8.2m Optus receipt, and it reflects NIL income tax paid in FY2026 against $12.7m in FY2025. This model therefore uses underlying revenue and EBITDA, Sky's own normalised free cash flow, and a normal 28% NZ tax rate throughout.
valuation_philosophy.income_vs_growth: This is an income stock, not a growth stock, and it should be valued as one. The core Sky Box satellite base has fallen from 514,982 customers in FY2023 to 422,000 in FY2026 - roughly 5-8% a year - and represents the majority of revenue. FY2026's +9.9% revenue growth was acquisition-driven, not organic. The growth products are real but small: Neon 252k (itself now shrinking, and facing a standalone HBO Max in NZ from 16 June 2026 after Sky declined to renew exclusivity), Sky Sport Now 159k, broadband 59k. Management's own FY2027 guidance of $825-840m revenue against FY2026 underlying $826.1m is, at the midpoint, +0.8% - essentially flat. The investment case rests on the ~9% fully-imputed dividend yield and a net cash balance sheet, not on compounding.
valuation_philosophy.dividend_sustainability: The 32 cps FY2026 dividend costs $44.1m. Against underlying EPS of 30.4c that is a payout of about 105% of underlying earnings - Sky is distributing slightly more than it earns on an underlying basis. It is more comfortable against cash: 74.9% of Sky's own normalised free cash flow of $58.9m, within the stated 60-90% policy band. FY2027 guidance of at least 35 cps ($48.2m) would be about 90% of this model's year-1 owner FCF of $53.5m - at the very top of that band. The dividend is therefore covered by cash but not by earnings, and it depends on capex staying inside the guided 6-8% of revenue envelope. It is fundable in the base case and comes under real pressure in the bear case, where owner FCF falls to $6m by year 10. Investors should treat the ~9% yield as a genuine but not risk-free return, with the 10%/yr growth target through FY29 dependent on synergy delivery.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: At $3.55 the probability-weighted intrinsic value of $3.49 is 1.7% BELOW the current price. The stock is fully valued. It trades near its 52-week high ($3.02-$3.66, 83% of the range) at ~1.05x book and ~2.6x EV/EBITDA - the top of a 10-year range in which Sky has NEVER traded above ~1.0x book. The base case alone offers +2.3%, and reaching it already requires a modest re-rating beyond anything the last decade has paid. The bull case (+62%) needs an advertising turnaround in a contracting linear market plus a margin above a target Sky has already missed twice; the bear case (-51%) needs only the current subscriber trend to continue and the fixed satellite cost base to deleverage. There is no manufactured upside here: the honest reading is that the market has already priced the Sky Free acquisition, the cheaper NZR deal and the dividend growth target, and a buyer at $3.55 is being compensated at roughly the 13% cost of equity and no more. The 15%-hurdle entry price is $3.21, about 10% below the current price.

methodology_notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, three probability-weighted scenarios.

Horizon is 10 years because the base-case owner-FCF margin is still moving at year 5 (6.4% -> 6.5%) as synergies land and then mix-shift erodes it; a 5-year cut would capitalise a transitional margin.
Terminal value = max(0, min(Gordon, exit-multiple cap x terminal EBITDA)). Gordon bound in all three scenarios; no scenario hit the zero floor.
Base terminal growth is 0.0% - deliberately NOT the usual 2-3%. A business whose majority revenue stream shrinks 5-8%/yr does not grow with GDP in perpetuity. Bear uses -1.0%, bull +1.0%.
Discounting is end-of-year, consistent with the rest of this folder.

Lease treatment (B) throughout: lease principal of ~3.16% of revenue is deducted inside the flows and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Sky's own 'normalised free cash flow' definition uses exactly this convention.

EBITDA column basis: the CSV EBITDA series is REPORTED/statutory for all 22 periods (FY2026 170.2, FY2025 120.6). The model uses UNDERLYING EBITDA (FY2026 157.0) as the base, sourced from the company's own reconciliation table.
